title: basis — one reading of one instrument
description:
How a derived value is known: which instrument was read, by whom, when, and — the load-bearing part — whether the instrument could look at all. This is the 'instrument silent ≠ resource absent' rule made structural. Today the same distinction is scattered across the substrate as `content_basis`, `stage_basis`, `date_basis`, `finished_at_basis`, `containment_omitted`, `observed_by`; this rider is the one shape they share.

Three states, each a different sentence: `read` = looked and saw something; `empty` = looked, and there was nothing there; `BLIND` = could not look (missing file, denied path, timeout, a classifier refusal). A reader MUST NOT conclude absence from BLIND — a transcript that was never on disk yields `turns: 0` and an empty page exactly as a silent session would, and only this rider tells them apart. Never conclude absence from output that already printed a denial: that tell is the control, failing.

Basis rides on DERIVED values (tier.json: machine-computed, reproducible). On a shed record it is a list, one entry per instrument shed read to draft the record — the transcript and git. An `evidence` block on an interpreted entry is the same idea at entry granularity: the instrument is the transcript, the reading is the quote, and the substring test is the reproduction.

instrument.description: What was read: `transcript`, `git`, a tool name, a device id, a URL. Free-form, but stable per writer so a reader can group readings.

state.description: read = looked and saw. empty = looked, nothing there. BLIND = could not look. A failed instrument never renders as a healthy or an unhealthy resource.

observer.description: Who or what did the reading: a tool id, a session sid8, a peer name. Unverified — a claim inside a claim.

observed_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC. When the instrument was read; a stale reading of a healthy resource is itself a failure to report.

detail.description: Free-form context, chiefly the reason behind BLIND (the error text, the denied path).
